items.markdown:
You likely get hangovers easily because of how your body processes alcohol, combined with habits, sleep, and the types of drinks you choose . Everyone's tolerance differs, and some people feel hungover after just one drink.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESsAEBxCJF15tEgC0Z0lH6SOjPoRVt9G_ip2zD9HJZc75JSWc0Qr0R6_TjnV5t2zo11YKO_4GUd2MorPiLM5Jz7ONlfhPFjSXp6b6sM_O7I1hGlw5HyLNkiC2ZaKPpoLjIfIxhoe7iaY6JT8PGUhzwbbU3BXf3K6N-4ciL8FfoFFBhFqjEbDs8oF6Gc1OrH3LHSdfOoXPJK0B3QlXsGsWo1uQh6Q7GwZU5VHKv64u3Tv7S5A)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF15SyBjdwqKaMBPJUDPXGLSvmei6pmFB_dCukE9JMztjeM4jQmGBpU1GD4EblhQWhfuvHxfsBniXyHiCMzz1g_bJ_UW0lBicxvIU7RKhbSzIY3DnQF2atqypeppGAD8OToaBAnNgvOfCAuW7zZKAve7pWym4kmo4jBfMfLv0Hb7FZeXoR7yXSS__Qi74)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXtHyTyqe3XJw_wcqCfJS_9UH8_RWb75UdvnWRlyo9-d0tv-de2hySIrBjQmviSCRXIK1PsuGCAM27cVNs8bbtVdTcmv8l7-bNZFHzYheV_TEj1Tr1vsQXZqdc3kznXRYtB0a9jQopETKkeAfBvKlqqPeQEw)

### Biological & Genetic Factors

- **Enzyme differences:** Your liver breaks alcohol down into acetaldehyde, a toxic compound, before clearing it out. Variations in enzymes (like ALDH2) can slow how fast acetaldehyde is cleared, causing stronger symptoms. There is a consensus on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF17U0MuGUd8VRtf4W9AXyMr-QnhT4-Xuc3x7lx4O1Vs4Jh4fz3e6nlNdh03bAUSFJiAuT5BFmKNjmCsBjK_wySNBLg6g6SHZSj8nmwQ6NUPEt-M8rZkCveDSdP3p_bd2AvAxHIcO3D7CxTdzSGtLMlvl-h-c4VaqObIhf4GZJURp2r1pkwJozWvUGz_W8WT4xshfd69rYT_M) that an alcohol flush reaction linked to slower acetaldehyde processing contributes to intense hangovers.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF17U0MuGUd8VRtf4W9AXyMr-QnhT4-Xuc3x7lx4O1Vs4Jh4fz3e6nlNdh03bAUSFJiAuT5BFmKNjmCsBjK_wySNBLg6g6SHZSj8nmwQ6NUPEt-M8rZkCveDSdP3p_bd2AvAxHIcO3D7CxTdzSGtLMlvl-h-c4VaqObIhf4GZJURp2r1pkwJozWvUGz_W8WT4xshfd69rYT_M)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXtHyTyqe3XJw_wcqCfJS_9UH8_RWb75UdvnWRlyo9-d0tv-de2hySIrBjQmviSCRXIK1PsuGCAM27cVNs8bbtVdTcmv8l7-bNZFHzYheV_TEj1Tr1vsQXZqdc3kznXRYtB0a9jQopETKkeAfBvKlqqPeQEw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESsAEBxCJF15tEgC0Z0lH6SOjPoRVt9G_ip2zD9HJZc75JSWc0Qr0R6_TjnV5t2zo11YKO_4GUd2MorPiLM5Jz7ONlfhPFjSXp6b6sM_O7I1hGlw5HyLNkiC2ZaKPpoLjIfIxhoe7iaY6JT8PGUhzwbbU3BXf3K6N-4ciL8FfoFFBhFqjEbDs8oF6Gc1OrH3LHSdfOoXPJK0B3QlXsGsWo1uQh6Q7GwZU5VHKv64u3Tv7S5A)
- **Inflammation:** Alcohol triggers immune responses and inflammatory chemicals (cytokines) that drive headaches, fatigue, body aches, and nausea.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1zoaoLE7qhu-dO9G3-9U5ekY4ew3UJP4-OOhCmjUgKJPPGhnjkIEjx_ySf-CzMgWHO9M2Z6tsBeDCcFDYm6eyGqYH4zncDz_9nWrzp93v5gUtz4KuZGtxc8Up5gDLS1WtwC026TNWQ9wMEzUwszZMZLW4eT5Y5AMj7Yh2GYmmE2LJFW_9Vm1vGHM9Ys)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1_iMtpjlVJaVAWt5WXYYlnLgzB7NtL_MpKxgwWjjdKQ5gSYsAXwk4-jpsWvGZt7see4RLd9I0oglp0s12jCJYGOnn2JNzQxNipMy9gNOaw6n_flTZ2kc85Wt2s-W1zjoZ-H1eXuVR6wUDq6FNwPSf8NXjtWyAEbqV27kw2N1IwSe)
- **Dehydration and blood sugar:** Alcohol suppresses vasopressin, increasing urination and fluid loss, and it can interfere with glucose release, contributing to weakness or shakiness.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1_iMtpjlVJaVAWt5WXYYlnLgzB7NtL_MpKxgwWjjdKQ5gSYsAXwk4-jpsWvGZt7see4RLd9I0oglp0s12jCJYGOnn2JNzQxNipMy9gNOaw6n_flTZ2kc85Wt2s-W1zjoZ-H1eXuVR6wUDq6FNwPSf8NXjtWyAEbqV27kw2N1IwSe)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfgHEIkXXOFq8mU7eP5kspe-vO46c7CVeiUYnVk-kjDh7E6ZhydqW7lpk-MFVyxpCqe_ckJfqixBAMcyl3i-z-vWOy1n6GafF7CcOgqPPxjN8rfgq6Q8gmPGSgYSYxwEolo3ACRPwuyDWE4HeY_jbY7LwJsPrQ57b5ivbKTOQqw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXwIQUDi-I3VF4YAW-MMQgHTLCszLEiEJy5eFQjeNWzubPgEln2Me08YS-nJ3OcFqdDRHgNObuk2UrPJbZpxMD1A0k-vKCb5v3mmLgQ0REN64AEVjYQUcBKCFY5fLS8pRijg)
- **Family history:** Having close relatives with alcohol use disorder can point to inherited differences in how your body handles alcohol.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF15SyBjdwqKaMBPJUDPXGLSvmei6pmFB_dCukE9JMztjeM4jQmGBpU1GD4EblhQWhfuvHxfsBniXyHiCMzz1g_bJ_UW0lBicxvIU7RKhbSzIY3DnQF2atqypeppGAD8OToaBAnNgvOfCAuW7zZKAve7pWym4kmo4jBfMfLv0Hb7FZeXoR7yXSS__Qi74)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXtHyTyqe3XJw_wcqCfJS_9UH8_RWb75UdvnWRlyo9-d0tv-de2hySIrBjQmviSCRXIK1PsuGCAM27cVNs8bbtVdTcmv8l7-bNZFHzYheV_TEj1Tr1vsQXZqdc3kznXRYtB0a9jQopETKkeAfBvKlqqPeQEw)

### Drink Choices & Drinking Habits

- **Drinking faster than your body clears alcohol:** The body takes roughly an hour to process one drink, so having more than one per hour raises your risk.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXtHyTyqe3XJw_wcqCfJS_9UH8_RWb75UdvnWRlyo9-d0tv-de2hySIrBjQmviSCRXIK1PsuGCAM27cVNs8bbtVdTcmv8l7-bNZFHzYheV_TEj1Tr1vsQXZqdc3kznXRYtB0a9jQopETKkeAfBvKlqqPeQEw)
- **Drinking more than usual:** Having noticeably more than your typical amount can trigger a hangover even if the total isn't extreme.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF16p1L-ExZMvWQNx211S7S5duWWotIYu8j0YEds8xDTheuxEPm_3wYiLkmP53EtP3xF60z3nHXoEeB2FsvmQ_p2dvi79oFr8Yzjld32iym7YdxVCPSvzliffCxhxTzeRrBlQuCSQiTf99EvAPhfs4OX7kmU78x2LgJdKxUmLseQ)
- **Empty stomach:** Food slows how quickly alcohol enters your bloodstream.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF15SyBjdwqKaMBPJUDPXGLSvmei6pmFB_dCukE9JMztjeM4jQmGBpU1GD4EblhQWhfuvHxfsBniXyHiCMzz1g_bJ_UW0lBicxvIU7RKhbSzIY3DnQF2atqypeppGAD8OToaBAnNgvOfCAuW7zZKAve7pWym4kmo4jBfMfLv0Hb7FZeXoR7yXSS__Qi74)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXtHyTyqe3XJw_wcqCfJS_9UH8_RWb75UdvnWRlyo9-d0tv-de2hySIrBjQmviSCRXIK1PsuGCAM27cVNs8bbtVdTcmv8l7-bNZFHzYheV_TEj1Tr1vsQXZqdc3kznXRYtB0a9jQopETKkeAfBvKlqqPeQEw)
- **Darker drinks (congeners):** Bourbon, whiskey, brandy, and red wine have higher levels of congeners—fermentation byproducts that can make hangovers worse than clear spirits like vodka or gin (though any alcohol can cause one).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXBBXQukdZpCpA2C1pXuxc0ZRNQihCCKPLrybT1sLD7i_hCeucmG2y5ciGsig7_oLI0G9CImO8dfuo1MN-qw7UH4NHzEmjl0uCfWr_TkgJ-xJeQAvKRN_VJXmcrnNFqDi34g584gVd)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF15SyBjdwqKaMBPJUDPXGLSvmei6pmFB_dCukE9JMztjeM4jQmGBpU1GD4EblhQWhfuvHxfsBniXyHiCMzz1g_bJ_UW0lBicxvIU7RKhbSzIY3DnQF2atqypeppGAD8OToaBAnNgvOfCAuW7zZKAve7pWym4kmo4jBfMfLv0Hb7FZeXoR7yXSS__Qi74)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXtHyTyqe3XJw_wcqCfJS_9UH8_RWb75UdvnWRlyo9-d0tv-de2hySIrBjQmviSCRXIK1PsuGCAM27cVNs8bbtVdTcmv8l7-bNZFHzYheV_TEj1Tr1vsQXZqdc3kznXRYtB0a9jQopETKkeAfBvKlqqPeQEw)
- **Other substances:** Nicotine, marijuana, or other substances used alongside alcohol can worsen hangover symptoms.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXtHyTyqe3XJw_wcqCfJS_9UH8_RWb75UdvnWRlyo9-d0tv-de2hySIrBjQmviSCRXIK1PsuGCAM27cVNs8bbtVdTcmv8l7-bNZFHzYheV_TEj1Tr1vsQXZqdc3kznXRYtB0a9jQopETKkeAfBvKlqqPeQEw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF16p1L-ExZMvWQNx211S7S5duWWotIYu8j0YEds8xDTheuxEPm_3wYiLkmP53EtP3xF60z3nHXoEeB2FsvmQ_p2dvi79oFr8Yzjld32iym7YdxVCPSvzliffCxhxTzeRrBlQuCSQiTf99EvAPhfs4OX7kmU78x2LgJdKxUmLseQ)

### Sleep Disruption

- Even if alcohol helps you fall asleep faster, it fragments sleep later in the night and reduces sleep quality. Short or broken sleep overlaps heavily with hangover fatigue, grogginess, and trouble concentrating.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF15SyBjdwqKaMBPJUDPXGLSvmei6pmFB_dCukE9JMztjeM4jQmGBpU1GD4EblhQWhfuvHxfsBniXyHiCMzz1g_bJ_UW0lBicxvIU7RKhbSzIY3DnQF2atqypeppGAD8OToaBAnNgvOfCAuW7zZKAve7pWym4kmo4jBfMfLv0Hb7FZeXoR7yXSS__Qi74)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1_iMtpjlVJaVAWt5WXYYlnLgzB7NtL_MpKxgwWjjdKQ5gSYsAXwk4-jpsWvGZt7see4RLd9I0oglp0s12jCJYGOnn2JNzQxNipMy9gNOaw6n_flTZ2kc85Wt2s-W1zjoZ-H1eXuVR6wUDq6FNwPSf8NXjtWyAEbqV27kw2N1IwSe)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF16p1L-ExZMvWQNx211S7S5duWWotIYu8j0YEds8xDTheuxEPm_3wYiLkmP53EtP3xF60z3nHXoEeB2FsvmQ_p2dvi79oFr8Yzjld32iym7YdxVCPSvzliffCxhxTzeRrBlQuCSQiTf99EvAPhfs4OX7kmU78x2LgJdKxUmLseQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXyURkFVbOlkiuedwmunVfhtdeYRGPrG6yPJSgrLhzApKF1_PAaMjoeBiH17pnUYgiE-02PfcLQLneFUKX8O3cabMdgzVHqSBLFzDNd4RfUmnopgi5NYzJE8mqyx9iuv0w68cpIk6KRw)

For more details on symptoms, prevention, and myths, see the [National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1_iMtpjlVJaVAWt5WXYYlnLgzB7NtL_MpKxgwWjjdKQ5gSYsAXwk4-jpsWvGZt7see4RLd9I0oglp0s12jCJYGOnn2JNzQxNipMy9gNOaw6n_flTZ2kc85Wt2s-W1zjoZ-H1eXuVR6wUDq6FNwPSf8NXjtWyAEbqV27kw2N1IwSe) hangover guide.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1_iMtpjlVJaVAWt5WXYYlnLgzB7NtL_MpKxgwWjjdKQ5gSYsAXwk4-jpsWvGZt7see4RLd9I0oglp0s12jCJYGOnn2JNzQxNipMy9gNOaw6n_flTZ2kc85Wt2s-W1zjoZ-H1eXuVR6wUDq6FNwPSf8NXjtWyAEbqV27kw2N1IwSe)If you want to narrow this down, share:

items.title: Biological & Genetic Factors
items.text: Enzyme differences: Your liver breaks alcohol down into acetaldehyde, a toxic compound, before clearing it out. Variations in enzymes (like ALDH2) can slow how fast acetaldehyde is cleared, causing stronger symptoms. There is a consensus on Reddit that an alcohol flush reaction linked to slower acetaldehyde processing contributes to intense hangovers. Inflammation: Alcohol triggers immune responses and inflammatory chemicals (cytokines) that drive headaches, fatigue, body aches, and nausea. Dehydration and blood sugar: Alcohol suppresses vasopressin, increasing urination and fluid loss, and it can interfere with glucose release, contributing to weakness or shakiness. Family history: Having close relatives with alcohol use disorder can point to inherited differences in how your body handles alcohol.

items.title: Drink Choices & Drinking Habits
items.text: Drinking faster than your body clears alcohol: The body takes roughly an hour to process one drink, so having more than one per hour raises your risk. Drinking more than usual: Having noticeably more than your typical amount can trigger a hangover even if the total isn't extreme. Empty stomach: Food slows how quickly alcohol enters your bloodstream. Darker drinks (congeners): Bourbon, whiskey, brandy, and red wine have higher levels of congeners—fermentation byproducts that can make hangovers worse than clear spirits like vodka or gin (though any alcohol can cause one). Other substances: Nicotine, marijuana, or other substances used alongside alcohol can worsen hangover symptoms.

items.title: Sleep Disruption
items.text: Even if alcohol helps you fall asleep faster, it fragments sleep later in the night and reduces sleep quality. Short or broken sleep overlaps heavily with hangover fatigue, grogginess, and trouble concentrating.
